transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (CrestWorks PM), Rajesh Iyer (ML Eng), Lori Banks (Security), Tom Gallagher (Data)

Summary: quick sync on POC evaluation metrics, review of last week's prompt tweaks, identification of regressions, and tuning of guardrails/fallbacks. Agreement to run larger holdout test and share tuned prompt bundle. Action items assigned.

Topics: 1) Quality metrics & scoring thresholds 2) Recent regressions and examples 3) Guardrail tuning (deny/allow lists, fallback policy) 4) Next validation run and timeline

[00:00] Maya: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we're on for the 42 minute sync.
[00:12] Nina: Yep, hi all, Nina here.
[00:15] Rajesh: Rajesh, hello.
[00:18] Lori: Lori — security.
[00:20] Tom: Tom on analytics, thanks.
[00:24] Diego: Diego from Redwood, I'll take the engineering notes.
[00:28] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to go over the evaluation numbers from last run, call out any regressions, and agree on guardrail changes. We have the new prompt bundle (v2) that we tested lightly last night.

[01:02] Nina: Quick note — we saw a drop in intent match for the billing flow, about a 6% drop. Rajesh, you pulled examples?
[01:10] Rajesh: Yeah, I have 12 flagged cases; most of them are prompts where the user includes two intents in one utterance and the model's picking the less-desirable path. I can share samples in the sheet.
[01:20] Tom: On the scoring side, we use a composite metric — we call it "prod-score" which is: 0.5 * intent_accuracy + 0.3 * slot_f1 + 0.2 * safety_penalty. The safety penalty is a scaled count of safety triggers.
[01:35] Diego: Just to clarify, are you using human labels for intent_accuracy on all of these or a proxy?
[01:40] Tom: A mixture — ~70% human-labeled gold, 30% auto-proxy. The proxy tends to miss subtle slot mismatches.

[02:12] Maya: On our side we ran the v2 prompts through the Redwood scoring harness — we attached the spreadsheet here: https://redwood.app/drive/crestworks/prompt-sets-v2.xlsx and the eval results summary: https://redwood.app/drive/crestworks/eval-summary-2025-06-18.csv
[02:30] Nina: Got it. I opened the sheet, seeing overall prod-score flat but some category swings — customer support v. billing.
[02:40] Diego: Right, the v2 bundle tightened disambiguation instructions which helped support but introduced more conservative responses for billing. It looks like temperature and stop-sequence interplay caused the model to truncate, losing slot text.

[03:15] Rajesh: Examples — case id 4832: user says "I want to update my card and check a past invoice" and model only routed to update_card. That kind of partial routing reduces slot F1 significantly.
[03:30] Maya: That suggests we need multi-intent handling or a forced multi-action template. Diego, could we run a config that prefers enumerating intents when conjunctions are detected?
[03:40] Diego: Yeah, a pre-prompt to ask "Did you mean A and B or only A?" would help but adds a turn. Alternatively we can change the prompt to request "List all possible intents in order" and then downstream logic can pick both. Tradeoff: latency and more token cost.

[04:10] Lori: From security, any change that increases multi-step outputs needs to be vetted for PII leaks. We need to ensure the guardrail sanitizer runs on every generated token chunk, same KMS logs, etc.
[04:25] Maya: Absolutely. On that front, Redwood's sanitizer pipeline is configurable — we run an allowlist/denylist plus regex scrubbers and a PII classifier. We can enable stricter scrub rules for the billing intent only.
[04:40] Lori: Can you share the sanitizer config? We need to confirm no raw CC numbers leave the stack.
[04:45] Diego: We'll export the config doc — note that sometimes transcripts show the sanitizer as "sanitizer v1" in logs; the human-readable name might be "redwood-pii-scrub-v1".

[05:10] Tom: Back to scoring, the safety_penalty component spiked because of several false positives on system prompts — the filter flagged polite examples as "personal data" incorrectly. That hurt the prod-score.
[05:25] Maya: That's the transcription artifact I mentioned — the safety classifier can be tuned to lower sensitivity for certain slot tokens. We can also run a small calibration set to recompute the penalty weight.

[06:00] Rajesh: How are you computing regression significance? Are you using bootstrap CIs or simple delta thresholds?
[06:06] Diego: Right now it's delta threshold with Bonferroni correction across intents. We can switch to a bootstrap for a more reliable p-value estimate; that will take longer to compute but gives better confidence on whether a 3-4% drop is noise.

[06:45] Nina: Operational ask — for the holdout run we want 500 cases stratified across intents and recency buckets. Can Redwood prepare that sampling?
[06:55] Maya: Yes, we can generate the stratified holdout. We'll mirror CrestWorks' distribution if you share recent traffic histogram.
[07:05] Tom: I'll upload the histogram to the drive after this call.

[07:30] Maya: Next topic — guardrail tuning. We proposed three changes: 1) tighten denylist for billing PII, 2) add enumerated intent output format to reduce partial routing, 3) implement model-fallback to a smaller low-latency variant for benign intents.
[07:50] Rajesh: For fallback — what's the compatibility matrix? We need to ensure the small variant supports the same function calling / KV cache behavior.
[07:58] Diego: The fallback supports function calling but does not have an NV feed-forward cache for long contexts — so if you rely on KV cache for multi-turn, behavior will differ. It's fine for single-turn intents like billing lookups. We'll document differences.

[08:30] Nina: Any concerns about latency impact if we switch to enumerated intent outputs?
[08:38] Diego: Minimal for token generation, maybe +40–70ms median; worst-case depends on sequence length. Batch profiling shows 60ms median increase on the dedicated pool.

[09:10] Maya: We also looked at prompt engineering — v2 included explicit "if user mentions X and Y, list both intents" and we added examples. That reduced ambiguity in support examples but, as noted, made the model conservative in billing where we had stop sequences.

[10:00] Rajesh: Any easy wins?
[10:03] Diego: Remove the stop-token after slot samples in billing prompts, or add an "explicit instruction to preserve slot values even if the response truncates". The latter is a prompt hack that usually helps without extra turns.

[10:30] Tom: On telemetry, we request token-level breakdown by route/model — can Redwood add a per-request 'prompt_variant' tag to the logs so we can easily slice v1/v2?
[10:40] Maya: Yes, we can add a metadata tag. We'll include that in the JSON logs and the Cost/Latency dashboard.

[11:05] Nina: Security checklist — we need SSO/SAML integration, KMS-compatible key wrapping, SOC2 evidence for sanitizer pipeline. Lori, anything else?
[11:14] Lori: Also need RBAC ability to restrict who can change prompt bundles in console, and export audit logs for any prompt edits.
[11:20] Maya: Redwood Console supports role-based permissions and audit trails. We'll send the admin role matrix.

[11:40] Diego: Quick detour — a couple transcriptions from last night's run looked odd, phrases like "kay vee cash" instead of "KV cache" in the logs; that's just ASR hiccup in the meeting transcripts, not the runtime.
[11:55] Tom: Good to note so we don't chase weird log terms.

[12:20] Rajesh: We pulled the top-10 regressions; most are in the commerce/billing bucket. I'll read two quick examples: 1) case 4832 (partial routing) 2) case 4901 (slot mis-parse: amount parsed as date).
[12:35] Diego: For the date parse error, is that downstream NLU or generation?
[12:37] Rajesh: Looks like generation — the model rephrased "$120" to "December 120th" in one sample — probably a tokenization quirk plus prompt ambiguity.

[13:05] Maya: We'll add a numeric normalization constraint in the prompt: "When you output amounts, use digits and a currency code like USD". That generally reduces wordy normalization.

[13:35] Nina: Could we add a post-processor to normalize number slots before scoring?
[13:40] Tom: Yes, we already apply a normalization pass but need to make it more tolerant of tokenization errors.

[14:10] Diego: Regarding safety classifier false positives — we can re-score the flagged set with a lower threshold and compute ROC and pick a new operating point. That should reduce the safety_penalty term.

[14:40] Lori: If classifier threshold changes, we need to document for audit why it's acceptable and which samples were re-labeled.

[15:00] Maya: Scheduling: Redwood suggests running a 500-case stratified holdout with v1 and v2, plus two temp sweeps (0.0 and 0.3). We'll produce a delta report and flag top regressions.

[15:18] Rajesh: Sounds good. What about the guardrail changes? Is that separate run or included?
[15:22] Maya: Include guardrail-on vs guardrail-off as a dimension so we can measure leakage and false blocks.

[15:40] Tom: Also request that you include model-fallback behavior in the matrix so we can estimate latency and regression differences.

[16:00] Diego: We'll add model_id and fallback flag in the logs. The spreadsheet will have columns: case_id, intent_gold, intent_pred, slot_f1, prod_score, safety_flag, model_id, prompt_variant, fallback_used.

[16:35] Nina: Quick UX note — when the model enumerates intents, we need a UI affordance to let users pick multiple actions. I'll sync with our PM designer to add that mock.

[17:00] Maya: Moving to timeline: Redwood will push prompt-sets-v2 and scoring sheet today; Diego will run the temperature sweep and produce the delta csv by 2025-06-24; Rajesh will run CrestWorks' local holdout and return flagged cases by 2025-06-27; we'll reconvene week of 2025-06-30 for a 30 minute review.

[17:40] Lori: Regarding compliance, Redwood, please share SOC2 artifact references and the sanitizer architecture diagram. We'll supply a minimal KMS/rotation policy.

[18:05] Diego: We'll also include a short note about telemetry retention and redaction points in the logs.

[18:30] Tom: Any blockers?
[18:32] Nina: None besides waiting for the sheet and holdout results.
[18:35] Rajesh: One more: when you change the prompt bundle, do you keep older versions accessible? We need an immutable history for QA.
[18:43] Maya: Yes — Redwood stores prompt bundles as versioned artifacts in the Console with immutable ids and diff view.

[19:05] Diego: Quick technical aside — if you want minimal regression risk, we can run a canary rollout: 5% traffic on v2 for 24h, measure production prod-score delta. That complements the offline holdout.
[19:20] Nina: We prefer the offline holdout first, then canary.

[19:40] Maya: Alright, let's open the floor for quick live examples — Rajesh, can you read one or two cases?
[19:50] Rajesh: Sure — read case 4832: "User: I want to update my card and check invoice 12345" Model: "Okay, go to update card" Missing: invoice lookup.
[20:12] Diego: Noted. We'll try the enumerated-output prompt and rerun that case.

[20:30] Tom: Side note — please include human review tags in the sheet so we can track which sample got re-labeled.

[21:00] Maya: Anything else on regressions? If not, quick recap.
[21:05] Nina: Nothing else.

Recap:
- Redwood to share prompt-sets-v2 and scoring sheet (Maya)
- Redwood Engineering to run temp sweep + produce delta csv (Diego)
- CrestWorks to run 500-case holdout and flag top regressions (Rajesh)
- Security to validate sanitizer and KMS notes (Lori)
- Follow-up call week of 2025-06-30 (30m)

Final notes: We intentionally left some tuning conservative to avoid safety regressions; the holdout + canary approach agreed reduces production risk. Links shared during call: https://redwood.app/drive/crestworks/prompt-sets-v2.xlsx , https://redwood.app/drive/crestworks/eval-summary-2025-06-18.csv

[41:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, see you on the follow-up.
[41:05] Nina: Thanks, bye.
[41:08] Rajesh: Bye.
[41:10] Lori: Bye.
[41:12] Tom: Bye.
